subject: Performance profile request: burst traffic patterns, KV cache impact, and fallback tolerances
messages:
From: Alice Streep <alice.streep@stratusfin.com>
To: Hiro Tanaka <hiro@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: performance profile for burst traffic and fallback tolerances

Hi Hiro,

Thanks for taking this — Stratus is finalizing an evaluation for a user-facing assistant that needs to survive large, unpredictable bursts. Before we lock scope for the PoC, can you provide a concise performance profile and proposed test methodology that addresses the following?

- Typical request mix: mixture of short completion calls (~16 tokens output), medium dialogs (~150 tokens), and long generative jobs (~1024 tokens). We'll approximate the mix as 60/30/10.
- Burst behavior: our traffic spikes from baseline ~30 qps to sustained bursts of 400–600 qps for 90–300s during business hours.
- Tail objectives: p95 < 100ms for short calls, p99 < 250ms for short/medium in normal operations; acceptable graceful degradation behavior during overload.
- KV cache: we plan to use prefix caching for session state — curious how effective this is across cold starts and multi-node serving.
- Cost sensitivity: we need a sense of incremental cost under different batching/quantization strategies and recommended fallback policies.

Please send a single document that: (a) outlines the test matrix you would run; (b) enumerates metrics and instrumentation we'd collect; (c) describes expected fallback modes (e.g., model variant, degraded token limit, queued responses); and (d) lists artifacts you can provide (scripts, config, synthetic traces).

Can you share this by EOD Monday PST? We want to attach it to our procurement packet.

Best,
Alice

Alice Streep
Director, Platform Engineering
Stratus Financial

From: Hiro Tanaka <hiro@redwood.com>
To: Alice Streep <alice.streep@stratusfin.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: performance profile for burst traffic and fallback tolerances

Alice — thanks, this is exactly the right level of detail. Below is an executive summary plus the proposed test matrix. I attached the runnable artifacts we usually share for PoCs.

Executive summary (short):
- We validate three operating regions: baseline steady-state, short-duration burst (30–300s), and sustained elevated load (>10min). For your burst sizes (400–600 qps) we recommend a hybrid of live traffic replay (if available) and synthetic burst injection to measure burst absorption, tail latency, and recovery.
- KV prefix caching typically reduces effective compute for medium/short dialogs by 20–60% depending on reuse locality; benefits are largest when request affinity pins sessions to the same serving shard. Cold-starts and cross-shard routing reduce effectiveness and should be included in the matrix.
- Graceful degradation: first line is an immediate fallback to a smaller/quantized model variant (1.5–3x cheaper) with token-limited responses; second line is progressive shedding (reject/queue low-priority requests) with informative 503+Retry-After semantics.

Proposed test matrix (high level):
1) Traffic profiles
   - Replay: 1:1 replay of representative production traces (if Stratus can provide).
   - Synthetic: Poisson baseline + scheduled bursts (sudden ramp, staircase, sawtooth) at 2x, 5x, and 10x baseline.
   - Request mix: run with 60/30/10 short/medium/long mixes; run single-class sweeps to isolate behavior.

2) Concurrency & batching sweeps
   - Concurrency sweep per model variant: 1, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100 concurrent request slots per GPU.
   - Batching knob: max-batch-size and batching window (0–50ms) combinations to capture latency/cost tradeoffs.

3) KV cache scenarios
   - Warm cache (95% hit rate simulated), mixed (50% hit), cold first-request.
   - Cross-shard routing simulation to show degradation in cache hit rate.

4) Fallback & degradation tests
   - Immediate model-variant fallback under threshold breach.
   - Token-limited fallback: measure utility loss (e.g., ROUGE/QA recall on small eval set).
   - Queuing/backpressure: measure queue depth, max wait, and Retry-After correctness.

5) Metrics & instrumentation to collect
   - Latency: p50/p95/p99/p999 for request wall time and per-component (queue, wait, decode).
   - Throughput: qps, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, memory usage, kernel stalls.
   - Error signals: 4xx/5xx rates, fallback counts, dropped/expired requests.
   - Resource metrics: per-host GPU RAM, PCIe saturation, CPU busy%, network Qdisc drops.

Artifacts we will provide
- Synthetic driver scripts and container images (burst-modes-simplan.xlsx included as a runbook + load schedule).
- KV cache impact report template (kv-cache-impact-runbook.pdf) with recommended warmup strategy.
- Fallback playbook (redwood-fallback-playbook.docx) describing policy thresholds and expected customer-visible behaviors.

Estimated timeline
- Draft test plan and artifacts: 2 business days.
- PoC execution (one week) to run matrix and collect evidence, dependent on availability of replay traces.
- Consolidated results and recommendations: 10 business days from test start.

Cost sensitivity notes (short):
- Quantized variants and aggressive batching reduce unit token cost but increase p99 risk; we typically recommend per-route SLOs to permit more aggressive cost settings on lower-priority routes.
- Dedicated capacity for steady-high qps offers predictable unit economics vs. bursty-on-demand where egress/burst pricing applies. We will include an incremental cost table in the deliverable.

Next steps
- If you can share a 24–72h representative trace, we will include a replay-run in the baseline. Otherwise we will recommend a synthetic schedule approximating your described spikes.
- Confirm whether the PoC should include dedicated capacity so we can model committed-vs-on-demand economics.

Attaching the artifacts referenced above. Happy to hop on a 30m call to walk through the plan.

—
Hiro Tanaka
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
hiro@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: burst-modes-simplan.xlsx (run schedule), kv-cache-impact-runbook.pdf, redwood-fallback-playbook.docx

Looping in a quick commercial note for visibility — Alice, happy to include a short appendix that maps the technical scenarios to commercial options (Hosted on-demand vs Dedicated reserved pools). Two asks:

1) Please include an explicit canary rollout suggestion for production (percent traffic, ramp step, rollback criteria).
2) Include a one-page summary of estimated incremental cost by fallback mode (quantized model, reduced token limit, queued/async responses).

Hiro — small edit request: in the test matrix, can you add a short-run that simulates "session affinity loss" where 15–25% of requests get routed to a different shard to show the KV cache sensitivity curves? That will be key for Stratus's architecture.

Thanks — I can prep the commercial appendix once we have the numbers.

Marissa
Director, Field Solutions, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
